text_blocks.snippet: Antipsychotic medications are used to treat mental health conditions like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and other psychotic disorders. They work by affecting neurotransmitters in the brain, primarily dopamine and serotonin. Common examples include risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, and aripiprazole, which are often referred to as atypical antipsychotics. First-generation antipsychotics, like haloperidol, are also available but may have different side effect profiles.
